content.overview: Clean stock is a controlled evidence state, not a visual compliment or a permanent biological guarantee. Specialists preserve identity and separate what is known from what remains unverified.

vocabulary.definition: Plant material managed through defined identity, health, testing and release controls.
A controlled designation such as quarantine, hold, eligible for use or released.

sections.title: Identity and health answer different questions
sections.body: A correct cultivar or accession label does not establish health status, and healthy appearance does not prove identity. Both records must remain linked through every transfer.

sections.title: Test results have a sample and time boundary
sections.body: A result applies to the identified sample, method and collection context. It does not certify every tissue or every future propagation generation.

sections.title: Release requires defined evidence
sections.body: A release decision should identify the required source record, status checks, testing context, reviewer authority and unresolved limitations. Missing evidence produces a hold or escalation, not an inferred pass.

workedExamples: A donor with a matching label but an unresolved genealogy gap remains an identity hold even if it looks vigorous.
A negative result from one dated sample supports that controlled decision point but is not a lifetime pathogen-free claim.
commonMistakes: Using healthy appearance as proof of clean-stock status.
Treating a negative test as permanent clearance.
Releasing material when identity or sample linkage is incomplete.
content.practicalApplication: Build a status board for six propagation lots showing source identity, sample linkage, test state, observations, holds, authorized reviewer and the evidence required for the next transition.
content.summary: Clean-stock control keeps identity, health observations, testing evidence and release authority separate but traceably connected.
